subject: CloudStash: planned analytics subprocessor add (SignalBridge) - notice and evidence ask
messages:
From: CloudStash Legal <legal@cloudstash.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: addition of SignalBridge as analytics subprocessor

Hi Kimberly / Jordan / Marissa,

Hope you are well — quick heads-up from CloudStash. We are adding SignalBridge (signalbridge.io) to our processing roster to provide aggregated analytics for our telemetry pipeline. SignalBridge will process pseudonymized telemetry aggregates derived from request metadata for performance analytics. No customer PII is included in the feed; only hashed identifiers, timestamps, and service-level metrics.

Effective date: 15 Oct 2026 (target).
Processing locations: EU (Poland), backup in IE.
Primary changes: lightweight aggregation, 90-day rolling retention for aggregated metrics.

Attached: CloudStash_Subprocessor_Notice_20260904.pdf (one-page notice with high-level scope).

If you have any objections or need evidence (SOC reports, dataflow diagrams, KMS attestations), let us know within 30 days and we will prioritize the package. Otherwise we'll consider this an approved notice and proceed with onboarding.

Thanks,
Pauline Meyer
Head of Legal — CloudStash

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Notice: addition of SignalBridge as analytics subprocessor

Team — forwarding the notice from CloudStash. Quick assessment: surface-level description seems fine but we need the usual evidence bundle before we mark as approved. Please see initial asks below; I want to send a consolidated request to Pauline today.

Requested evidence (initial):
- SOC 2 Type II report for SignalBridge (or equivalent assurance)
- Dataflow diagram showing exactly what leaves CloudStash and how it is pseudonymized
- Subprocessor inventory CSV (fields: name, role, country, data categories)
- KMS/Encryption handling summary (who holds keys; HSM/KMS provider)
- Retention and deletion policy for aggregates
- Onshore fallback plan (in case EU processing is interrupted)

Jordan / Ben: any additional redlines or must-haves? Lauren: can you prepare the evidence checklist template we usually send? Marissa: flag if this intersects any active procurement/contract work we have with CloudStash.

Kimberly
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Adding two quick asks from infra/security perspective:
1) Key custody: need clarity on whether SignalBridge will ever have access to un-hashed identifiers or if hashing occurs client-side at CloudStash before transit. If SignalBridge holds keys, we need HSM attestations and KMS region boundaries.
2) Contractual constraints: ensure there is a subprocessor addendum that limits use to analytics only and prohibits re-identification attempts. If CloudStash's contract doesn't already cover that, request an annex.

I'll coordinate with Security to flag any high-severity items, but first pass looks low risk provided the above are satisfied.

-Ben
Senior Security Engineer

Subject: RE: Notice: addition of SignalBridge as analytics subprocessor — evidence request

Hi Pauline — thanks for the notice and the heads-up. To complete our internal review we'd appreciate the following artifacts by close of business 2026-09-18: 

1) Latest SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent assurance for SignalBridge (or CloudStash's assessment if they absorb responsibility).
2) A detailed dataflow diagram (PDF) showing pseudonymization/hashing step and all fields transmitted.
3) Subprocessor inventory CSV (name, role, country, processing categories, effective date).
4) KMS/HSM summary: who controls keys, region of key storage, and whether SignalBridge can export cryptographic material.
5) Retention & deletion policy for aggregated metrics (exact retention periods and deletion guarantees).
6) Signed subprocessor addendum (or proposed contract annex) restricting processing purpose to analytics and prohibiting re-identification.
7) Onshore fallback plan (brief description) describing how processing will continue if EU endpoints are unavailable.

Attached is our standard subprocessor evidence checklist (subproc-evidence-checklist.xlsx) — please populate and return with the items above. If you cannot meet the deadline, tell us when you'll be able to provide the package. We may need to raise this with Procurement if any contract amendments are required.

Thanks — Lauren Bishop
Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: subproc-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Notice: addition of SignalBridge as analytics subprocessor — evidence request

Hi Lauren / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the checklist. We can provide everything you requested. A few notes:

- SignalBridge is a downstream analytics provider (no access to raw PII). Hashing is performed by CloudStash at the ingestion layer; SignalBridge receives only hashed ids.
- SOC 2 Type II for SignalBridge is available and we'll share the report via a secure link.
- KMS: keys are managed by CloudStash in AWS KMS (eu-west-1); SignalBridge encrypts its storage with their own KMS but does not hold CloudStash keys.
- Onshore fallback: CloudStash will failover to an EU onshore buffer (storage in FR) and replay to a different analytics endpoint if Poland is unavailable.

Secure share link (temporary): https://files.cloudstash.com/s/abc123 — contains the SOC 2, a populated subprocessor CSV, and a preliminary dataflow PDF. We'll follow up with the signed addendum; legal estimates 5–7 business days for that.

Let us know if anything in the packet triggers follow-up.

Best,
Pauline Meyer
Head of Legal — CloudStash
